FINDING-POSITIVE-THRESHOLD (verified, supports producer analysis): frozen positive-control pair is internally infeasible. Channel capacity for the frozen construction is I(L;L_next) = 1 - H_b(0.3) = 0.11871 bits (<0.5), confirmed by direct computation; DOM_before=SHA256(L||step_mod) is a 1-1 function of L within each stratum C=(URL,H_K,Action) because URL fixes step_mod, so the achievable CMI ceiling is exactly 0.1187 bits. Observed BC 0.0752 = 63.4% of that ceiling. The pipeline is NOT blind: raw p=0.001 (<0.005), Cohen d 4.92 (>2.0), delta 0.30 (>=0.10) all pass; only the BC>=0.5 magnitude gate fails. Producer's 'pipeline_blind' label is the frozen-rule clause name and is applied with accurate disclosure of the miscalibration — acceptable, but the label alone would mislead; the reason text carries the truth.

FINDING-POWER (new, more severe than producer discloses): no frozen configuration could have produced SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. The frozen primary threshold BC>=0.10 is also unreachable through the canonical positive mechanism at n=188 (noiseless proxy yields 0.075 < 0.10; even at capacity 0.119, the estimator recovers only ~63%). Unless production strata are much larger than frozen targets (10-15/stratum) or the estimator bias is corrected, the positive path of this design was structurally closed before outcome. Recalibration/power analysis is mandatory for the retry, not optional.

FINDING-NULL-DEGENERACY (verified): independent-noise synthetic null is degenerate: observed PMI 0.30560 = perm_mean with perm_std 5.55e-17 (~0), p=1.0 — the Laplace alpha=1.0 + Miller-Madow estimator has a +0.306-bit permutation-invariant bias floor when DOM hashes are near-unique per transition, so null_std>0.01 centering (frozen requirement) cannot be met. Frozen rule => MEASUREMENT_INVALID for that representation, correctly applied by producer. Structural hazard for the primary: production R1/R2 hash DOMs with session-unique content would occupy exactly this high-cardinality regime, so valid null centering on production hash DOMs is at risk as frozen (producer lists this in unresolved; it deserves fix-level status).
